a2-frequency.title: Frequency Adverbs
a2-frequency.pattern: doim (always) · tez-tez (often) · ba'zan (sometimes) · kamdan-kam (rarely) · hech qachon (never)
a2-frequency.explanation: Frequency adverbs sit before the verb they describe: men doim erta turaman (I always wake up early), u kamdan-kam kinoga boradi (he/she rarely goes to the movies). Hech qachon requires a negative verb to agree with it: hech qachon yolg'on gapirmayman (I never lie).
a2-frequency.fact: Hech qachon literally combines hech ("any/none at all") with qachon ("when") -- "never" in Uzbek is grammatically "at no when", and it always needs that negative verb alongside it, since a bare positive verb with hech qachon would be ungrammatical, not just unusual.

a2-postpositions.title: Postpositions: bilan, uchun, kabi
a2-postpositions.explanation: Uzbek uses postpositions -- separate words placed AFTER the noun -- instead of English-style prepositions: do'stim bilan (with my friend), sen uchun (for you), sher kabi (like a lion).
a2-postpositions.fact: Bilan can also fuse onto the noun as a suffix in fast speech (do'stimla for do'stim bilan is common informally), but uchun and kabi always stay separate words -- not every postposition in Uzbek is equally free to cliticize.

dialogue.en: It's for you, we chose it together with my friend.

items.en: We sometimes go to the movies.

items.uz: Sen hech qachon meni tashlab ketmaysan.

items.en: He/she is brave like a lion.
I went to the market with my mother.
This book was written for children.
He/she is free like a bird.

items.uz: Bu ish siz uchun juda muhim.
items.en: This matter is very important for you.
He/she is kind like my older brother.
This opportunity is beneficial for all of us.
